No text, border labels, logo or watermark.

A SINGLE worn tan skin body wrap, hair inward, overlapping front, both shoulders covered, sleeveless, irregular hem above knees, small repaired fold at anatomical LEFT shoulder, short chest tie BELOW throat, light cord at waist. The original narrow fox strip remains hidden UNDER LEFT shoulder; old bark waist layers and pelvic pad remain concealed. BOTH grass torso screens are stored and absent from body. Both original low woven bast soles, grass liners and low ties remain on feet; toes, ankles and lower legs exposed. No boots, leggings, trousers, extra cloak, metal, finished pot, bow, hafted spear or fletched dart. Exactly two natural arms and legs, readable hands, no overdeveloped heroic body. The head has ONLY the old low plain grey-brown rabbit crown pad, loose forehead/back band, ears and much nape exposed. It is worked fur, NOT a rabbit head: no animal ears, muzzle or face. No new cap flaps before Day 67.

Scene Day 65: man stands or half-crouches at the MOUTH of a shallow limestone overhang, hands checking one light retaining crosspiece on the newly extended low weather screen.
